title: Life-threatening limb bleeding (tourniquet last resort)
summary: Bleeding from an arm or leg that will not stop with hard pressure. A tourniquet is a last resort, used only when bleeding is life-threatening and direct pressure has failed.
steps: Call for emergency help immediately. This is a life-threatening situation.
Lay the person down and raise the bleeding limb above heart level if possible.
Press very firmly on the wound with the cleanest cloth you have. Keep pressing without lifting it to check.
If bleeding continues to soak through, add more cloth on top — never remove the first layer. Keep pressing.
Only if direct pressure fails and bleeding remains life-threatening: apply a wide band (5 cm or wider) about 5–7 cm above the wound, between the wound and the heart. Never on a joint.
Tighten the band until bleeding stops. Note the exact time it was applied — tell the medics that time.
Keep the person warm and reassure them. Do not loosen the tourniquet once placed.
avoid: Do not use a tourniquet for a small or moderate cut — direct pressure is safer and almost always enough.
Do not use a thin string, wire, or shoelace — they can cut tissue. Use a wide band only.
Do not place a tourniquet on the neck, torso, or directly over a joint.
Do not loosen, lift, or remove the tourniquet once it is on — only medical staff should do that.
Do not give the person food or drink in case surgery is needed.
whenToEscalate: Always — this is an emergency requiring hospital care immediately.
If signs of shock appear: pale, cold, clammy skin, fast weak pulse, drowsiness, or fainting.
If bleeding continues despite a tourniquet — keep direct pressure on the wound and get the person to an emergency department as fast as possible.
specialty: Emergency department or trauma centre — immediate transport.
